t: Sudan from Kerma to the Republic

stops.en: Rival of Egypt; Tuthmose I (−1530 to −1520 in GHA II) conquered the northern Sudan, ending the independence of the kingdom of Kush, and set up his great inscription at Tumbus (Tombos), the southern end of the Third Cataract.

cs.c: G. Mokhtar (ed.), UNESCO International Scientific Committee (1981) General History of Africa, II: Ancient Civilizations of Africa

stops.en: Kushite kings ruled Egypt as the 25th Dynasty; Shabaka 'brought the entire Nile valley as far as the Delta under the empire of Kush'.

cs.c: G. Mokhtar (ed.), UNESCO International Scientific Committee (1981) General History of Africa, II: Ancient Civilizations of Africa

stops.en: Kingdom centred on Old Dongola from the 6th c.; the baqt agreement with Muslim Egypt, followed by Abdallah ibn Abi Sarh's raid on Dongola in 651–2.

cs.c: K. Michałowski (1981) The spreading of Christianity in Nubia (General History of Africa II, ch.12)

stops.en: Suzerain over Upper Nubia above the Third Cataract, including the vassal kingdom of Dongola; Lower Nubia nominally under Ottoman Egypt.

cs.c: P.M. Holt & M.W. Daly (2011) A History of the Sudan: From the Coming of Islam to the Present Day

stops.en: Muhammad 'Ali conquered the disintegrating Funj lands in 1820–1; Ibrahim (GHA VI) calls this the 'first colonial era', ruled by a Turkish-speaking elite in the name of the Ottoman sultan.

cs.c: H.A. Ibrahim (with B.A. Ogot) The Sudan in the nineteenth century (General History of Africa VI, ch.14)

stops.en: A jihad movement that defeated Hicks at Shaykan (5 Nov 1883), took Kordofan, Darfur and Bahr al-Ghazal, and with 'Uthman Digna the east except Suakin; Khartoum fell and Gordon was killed (26 Jan 1885).

cs.c: H.A. Ibrahim (based on a contribution by Abbas I. Ali) African initiatives and resistance in North-East Africa (General History of Africa VII, ch.4)

stops.en: Declared a joint possession (condominium) of Britain and Egypt in January 1899 and in practice turned into a British colony; Egypt's parliament denounced the 1899 agreement on 15 Oct 1951.
Opened by the October 1964 civilian-led uprising that brought down Abboud's military regime, which GHA VIII calls exceptional in Africa.

cs.c: A.A. Mazrui (ed.) General History of Africa VIII: Africa since 1935 – Sudan passages ('North Africa and the Horn', pp.148–150; economy and political-succession passages)
